query: North Korea nuclear test 2026 - any signs of imminent 7th nuclear test, activity at Punggye-ri test site, recent statements or preparations mid-2026
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of my findings on signs of a potential 7th North Korean nuclear test as of late July 2026:

**Bottom line:** The Punggye-ri site is technically **ready** for a 7th test, but there are **no reported signs of imminent test preparations** in mid-2026.

**Key findings:**
- **Site readiness:** Tunnel No. 3 (restored ~May 2022) has been assessed as fully prepared for a test since 2020. US and South Korean intelligence consistently say Kim Jong Un could order a test on "short notice."
- **Latest imagery:** The most recent detailed satellite analysis (Daily NK, Nov 2025) found no instruments, cables, or personnel/vehicle activity indicating imminent testing — the site is in caretaker status.
- **Intelligence assessments:** US DNI Gabbard (March 2026) and the 2025 DIA report both describe North Korea as "postured" or "probably prepared" for a test at a time of its choosing. An April 2026 OSINT assessment estimates a test is "probable within 12–18 months."
- **Mid-2026 activity was about the broader program, not the test site:** June 3-4 unveiling of a new uranium enrichment plant; June 25-26 conventional weapons tests; and a July 27 Kim Yo Jong statement rejecting denuclearization ("ultimate shield," status "final and irreversible").
- **Notable nuance:** A Feb 2026 38 North analysis argues a 7th test may not be technically necessary given existing miniaturization — meaning any test would primarily be a **political signal**.

The consistent theme across all sources: **capability is ready; timing is a pending political decision, with no imminent signals observed** as of July 27, 2026. Full findings with sources and data points have been delivered via structured output.

key_facts: North Korea has not conducted a nuclear test since September 3, 2017 (its 6th test, a claimed two-stage thermonuclear/H-bomb device); a 7th test would be its first in nearly nine years.
Punggye-ri Tunnel No. 3 (South Portal) was restored around May 2022 and has remained usable; US and South Korea have assessed all preparations for a 7th test from Tunnel No. 3 as complete since 2020.
As of mid-2026, no open-source satellite imagery shows imminent test preparations (instrumentation, cabling, personnel/vehicle surge) at Punggye-ri; the site is in caretaker/maintenance status.
Nov 5, 2025: South Korea's Defense Intelligence Agency told lawmakers North Korea 'could carry out a nuclear test within a short period of time' at Tunnel No. 3 if Kim Jong Un orders it.
March 17, 2026: US DNI Tulsi Gabbard told the House Intelligence Committee North Korea is 'probably prepared to conduct another nuclear test on short notice.'
A 2025 US DIA report (cited in a May 29, 2026 CRS update) states North Korea 'has restored its nuclear test site and is now postured to conduct a seventh nuclear test at a time of its choosing.'
The 9th Congress of the Workers' Party of Korea (Feb 19-25, 2026) continued the nuclear/missile buildup but announced no nuclear test.

June 3-4, 2026: Kim Jong Un inspected a new weapons-grade nuclear material (uranium enrichment) plant, pledging to expand nuclear forces 'at an exponential rate' and claiming production capacity more than doubled over five years — a fissile-material development, not test-site activity.

July 27, 2026: Kim Yo Jong rejected the ASEAN Regional Forum's denuclearization call as a 'foolish attempt,' called nuclear weapons the 'ultimate shield,' declared North Korea's nuclear-state status 'final and irreversible,' and vowed the arsenal would be 'updated steadily.'

Analysts (38 North, Feb 2026) argue a 7th test may not be technically necessary given existing miniaturization; any test would likely serve as a political/strategic signal to validate the tactical Hwasan-31 warhead or a MIRV-compatible design.
An April 2026 OSINT assessment ranks a seventh nuclear test as 'probable within 12-18 months.'
Tunnels No. 1, 2, and 4 remain closed/collapsed; Tunnel No. 4 saw intermittent reactivation work in 2022-2023 but was never reopened.
